hints: Look at the steepness (gradient) of the curve, remember that gradient means rate, so notice how the rate first speeds up then slows down.
Consider why the rate speeds up from P to Q, the reaction is exothermic and magnesium is in large excess, so what factor could increase the rate?
Think about what runs out between Q and R to slow the rate down, with magnesium in large excess, which reactant concentration must be falling?
walkthrough:
**Read the rate from the graph**

The gradient of a volume against time graph is the rate of reaction. From P to Q the curve gets steeper, so the rate is increasing. From Q to R the curve flattens, so the rate is decreasing.

Rate rule:
$$\text{rate} = \text{gradient} = \frac{\Delta V}{\Delta t}$$

**Explain the speed up from P to Q**

Normally rate only falls as reactants are used up, so a speed up is unusual. Here the reaction is exothermic, so heat released warms the mixture.

Higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy and more successful collisions, so the rate increases. Magnesium surface area is actually falling a little, but that would slow the rate, not speed it up.

$$\text{Mg(s)} + 2\text{HCl(aq)} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)} \quad \Delta H < 0$$

**Explain the slow down from Q to R**

Later the temperature effect is outweighed by reactants being used up. The question states a large excess of magnesium ribbon is used.

That means magnesium cannot run out, so the dilute hydrochloric acid is the limiting reactant. Its concentration falls, so collision frequency falls and the rate decreases to zero at R.

options.A: Correct. P to Q rate increase is due to increasing temperature from the exothermic reaction. Q to R rate decrease is due to falling $\text{HCl}$ concentration, since $\text{Mg}$ is in large excess and cannot be used up.
options.B: Half right but half wrong. Temperature increase correctly explains P to Q, but magnesium cannot have been used up because the question clearly states a large excess of magnesium is present. The acid is the limiting reactant.
options.C: Incorrect for the first part. Decreasing surface area of magnesium would decrease collision frequency and decrease the rate, but the graph shows the rate is increasing between P and Q. Only increasing temperature explains the speed up.
options.D: Incorrect on both parts. Decreasing surface area would slow the reaction, not speed it up from P to Q, and magnesium in large excess is not used up by Q to R. This confuses which reactant is limiting.
